name: Lupin
grown_as: A hardy perennial border plant. Garden lupins are Russell hybrids (L. polyphyllus crosses, sometimes called Lupinus × regalis). The library has 'Gallery Blue', a compact variety about 50 cm with blue and white flowers: drawn as that. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: An upright clump: a mound of long-stalked leaves 40 to 60 cm across, with stiff upright flower spikes. 'Gallery' types 50 to 60 cm tall in flower; others up to 1.2 m. Grows from a deep taproot and woody crown; dies down in winter.

leaf.arrangement: Mostly from the base on long stalks, a few up the flower stems
leaf.type: Compound, palmate: 9 to 17 leaflets radiating from the top of the stalk like the spokes of a wheel
leaf.leaflets: All unstalked, alike and symmetrical, spread in a full circle or a little more than a half circle
leaf.outline: Each leaflet narrow lance-shaped, 4 to 12 cm
leaf.veins: A clear midrib; the leaflets often folded slightly along it
leaf.surface: Hairless or nearly so above, with flat silky hairs beneath; holds a drop of water at the centre after rain

flower.form: Many pea flowers in a long dense upright spike
flower.petals: Five: standard, wings and a curved pointed keel
flower.colour: 'Gallery Blue': mid violet-blue wings and keel with a white or white-marked standard. Other garden lupins in many colours.
flower.behind: A small two-lipped calyx; small bracts that fall early
flower.carried: In a tall dense spike 15 to 40 cm, the flowers in rings (whorls) round the stem, opening from the bottom up so buds are at the top, standing above the leaves
flower.size: Each flower 1.2 to 1.5 cm; spike 15 to 40 cm

fruit: Hairy pods 3 to 5 cm, standing out from the spike, green turning black, which twist and burst to throw out round, mottled grey-brown seeds 3 to 4 mm. Seeds poisonous.
seedling: Two thick, oval, fleshy seed leaves raised on a short stem, then a first true leaf already palmate with 5 to 7 small leaflets.
winter: Dies down to a crown at soil level, sometimes with a small tuft of new leaves

leaf: 9 to 17 narrow leaflets radiating from one point like wheel spokes
bloom: a tall dense spike of pea flowers in rings
blue wings with a white-marked standard
young: each leaf a wheel of narrow leaflets
flower: standing above the mound of palmate leaves
seedhead: spikes of hairy pods standing out from the stem
pods turning black, some twisted open
dormant: little or nothing green above ground

look_alikes: Tree lupin (Lupinus arboreus) is a shrub with yellow flowers. Wild Russell lupins along roads and rivers are the same plant gone wild. Hemp and horse chestnut leaves are palmate too but toothed.
